securityFindings.disposition: ACCEPTED_WITH_EVIDENCE: the digest is pinned in the record; the lookup's answer is recorded beside it
securityFindings.evidence: docker.io/library/node manifest by digest: HTTP 200, body sha256 == digest (read-only; nothing pulled)
securityFindings.finding: The container's base image was not pulled by this lane: it was already in the proving host's native engine (moved there by docker save/load in SP1-PA3B). Its identity is its content digest; its registry provenance rests on a read-only manifest lookup by that digest (nothing downloaded).

securityFindings.disposition: ACCEPTED: two independent TypeScript execution paths agreeing is part of the evidence
securityFindings.finding: The host derivation runs TypeScript through tsx from node_modules, installed from the npm registry by npm ci; the registry is a network dependency of the host path (integrity-pinned by package-lock.json). The container path has none: Node strips the types itself and a repository-owned hook resolves the two extensionless imports.

securityFindings.disposition: REPORTED: out of this lane's scope (no production tooling changed); an owner decision for the deployer
securityFindings.finding: The repository's deployer Dockerfile names its base image by tag (node:<version>-bookworm-slim, not a digest) and installs apt packages unpinned; docker-compose files reference walletwall-vault:latest. None of these is in the observer path; they are the Sepolia deployer's.

Raw captures hold host identity (addresses, boot id, exec paths, pids). The soaks' raw directories stay operator-local (root:prover-group, 0750) as SP1-PA3C's evidence model requires; only their digests and derivations are committed. The committed fixture remains the one privacy-reviewed capture.

securityFindings.disposition: CARRIED_FORWARD: owner decision HOST_LOCKFILE_REMEDIATION = DEFER_TO_NEXT_PROGRAM_REBUILD stands
securityFindings.finding: RustSec: zkvm/host/Cargo.lock still locks webpki-roots 1.0.7 (RUSTSEC-2026-0381) and rustls-webpki 0.103.13 (RUSTSEC-2026-0382), assessed CONDITIONAL / SHOULD_FIX_BEFORE_PRODUCTION in #233 (MUST_FIX 0). This lane compiles nothing with cargo, runs no SP1 host and opens no TLS connection: the exposure is unchanged, so the classification is carried forward, neither raised nor suppressed.

securityFindings.disposition: STATED: the host trust boundary is the proving host's root, as before
securityFindings.finding: The capture layer cannot be containerized without privileges: tracefs, kprobes and nftables act on the one shared WSL2 kernel, so the observer runs as root on the proving host and only the derivation is reproduced in the clean container. A hostile root on that host could edit a capture before it is derived (SP1-PA3C's trust statement). This qualification does not change that; it makes the derivation of whatever was captured reproducible anywhere.

securityFindings.disposition: CARRIED_FORWARD: the proving host's design, disclosed in SP1-PA3B and SP1-PA3C
securityFindings.finding: The proving user is in the docker group of the native engine, which is root-equivalent on the proving host (SP1-PA3C disclosed it); the container self-test is started by that user. Docker Desktop's own engine was stopped throughout and was not started or reset.

securityFindings.disposition: ACCEPTED_AS_MEASURED: the observer detected and attributed it; a SP1-PA3D run should expect refused attempts of other scopes (quieting chronyd first is an owner choice, not a requirement)
securityFindings.evidence: soak A: iterations 2 refused as EGRESS_LEAKED by another process; 11/12 refusal-free
securityFindings.finding: The proving host is not quiet: its own daemons egress during observation windows. Under the self-test table (TEST-NET-1 and the resolvers refused, nothing else) one soak iteration's capture was refused as EGRESS_LEAKED, as it must under a table that refuses no real egress: a KERNEL-scope attempt inside the window, and the frame it left through the uplink; the workload's own attempts were refused and reconciled as in every other iteration. The operator's inspection of that raw capture (operator-local, not committed) identified the sender as the host's chronyd sending one NTP datagram to a public time server; the committed derivation records the scopes and the refusal, not the process. Under the complete egress boundary (SP1-PA3B's, which SP1-PA3D runs under) the same traffic is refused, counted and attributed to another scope, never a leak.

unstableBecause: iteration 2 refused: EGRESS_LEAKED by another process (scope FRAME, KERNEL): the workload's own attempts were all refused
